Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

If f(x)=x² and g(x)=9, solve f(x)=g(x).

feedback.text: This forgets the negative square root.
Correct. x²=9 gives both the positive and negative square roots.
These do not both satisfy the equation.

Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

Which equation finds intersections of f and g?

feedback.text: This finds when the sum is zero.
Correct. Intersections have equal outputs for the same input.
This is not the general intersection condition.

feedback.text: The negative value is not viable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

Which representation is usually best for reading intervals of increase from a visual pattern?

feedback.text: A formula may help, but intervals are often clearest visually.
One point cannot show an interval.
A title does not show interval behavior.
Correct. Graphs show increasing and decreasing intervals visually.

Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.FN.3; MLA.A2.FN.11; MLA.A2.FN.12

If f(2)=7 and g(2)=7, what is true?

answer.text: The functions are equal for every input

feedback.text: One matching input does not prove that.
Correct. Equal outputs at the same input indicate an intersection.

Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q16

What does f(x)>g(x) mean on a graph?

feedback.text: Greater output means f is above g.
Correct. f has larger y-values than g for those inputs.

questiontext.text:

feedback.text: Correct. Zeros are x-values where y=0.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L07_Q18

feedback.text: Correct. Divide output change by input change.
